h1: Build a TikTok UGC Ad From a Product Link
lead: Launch a UGC-style TikTok ad in minutes, shaped for the format and the audience you already sell to.
summary: You leave with a tall TikTok ad, a spoken voice, captions, and one reason to buy.

sections.h2: A TikTok Ad You Can Post in Minutes
paras: You need one product and one reason to buy. The first TikTok ad is ready in minutes, with no filming day on the calendar.
Show the sunscreen tube and the cream going on, the way this photo does. Add a song you are allowed to use.
Use your own voice if the shop should sound like you. Or pick a generated voice and edit the line until it sounds like your counter.
You get captions, the tall shape, and a track from the music library. Send it to TikTok, or download it and post it yourself.
sections.alt: Adult woman applies sunscreen from a plain light-peach tube to her cheek at the seaside.

sections.h2: From a Product Link to a TikTok Ad
paras: Three moves, and you have a tall ad. No studio day, and no blank editor to figure out.
Paste the page that shows the sunscreen you ship. A page that leads with the tube is enough. Fix a wrong title before the job starts.
Or upload one photo and one sentence about the action. Add the price later, in the editor.
Match the picture here: a hand holds the peach tube over a notebook on a bright table.
Start from the product page, or start from a photo of the tube.
Pick the actor before you write the line, so the words fit that person. A product-only frame works too. See the [actor library](page:ai-actors). There are 53 AI actors.
The person on screen uses the look you picked, and the tube stays the one in your photo.
Play the tall file on your phone, then put the price in the editor. Publish to TikTok, or keep the download.
When a new listing goes up, your shop can start this same video from that page.
sections.alt: Adult hands hold a plain peach sunscreen tube over a blank notebook on a bright cafe table.

sections.h2: Skip the Film Crew on the First Ad
paras: The opening shows the cream doing something a shopper recognizes, while the tube stays in frame.
A first version can be a hand smoothing cream from the tube, with no influencer booked and no studio invoice.
The next opening can be a different first line on the same photo. You get that test without booking another morning.
A shop that also sells in another language can keep the scene and replace the spoken line. The scene stays the one you approved.
sections.alt: Two adult hands spread white sunscreen from a plain peach tube across the back of a hand.

sections.h2: Make More Versions From One Photo
paras: The tube is on screen while the shopper is still watching. That is the opening.
Keep the sunscreen photo. For the next file, change only who speaks. A new first line is its own test.

Match the length to the motion. Six seconds fits one motion. Ten fits a short demo. Fifteen fits a simple sequence. Thirty fits a longer one. A video is 24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, or 120 for 30.
Captions and the song live in this editor. When the words sit clear of the tube, this pass is done.
sections.alt: Adult hands hold a plain peach sunscreen tube by a bright window.

sections.h2: Where to Post the TikTok Ad
paras: The tall file is ready for TikTok. Each other placement gets the shape it actually plays, as its own file.
TikTok gets the 9:16 file, with the sunscreen on screen at the open. The [TikTok ads](page:plat-tiktok) page has the size detail.
Instagram Reels plays that same tall shape. [Instagram](page:plat-instagram) covers the feed next to Reels.
Facebook Reels stays tall, and the feed gets a square. See [Facebook](page:plat-facebook).
YouTube Shorts uses 9:16 again, with the words clear of the edges. [YouTube Shorts](page:plat-youtube-shorts) is that shape.
A product page on your store can hold the video where shoppers land after they tap.
A listing can show the same tube in a video beside the still. Sizes for every placement are in [ad sizes by platform](page:guide-ad-sizes-by-platform).
sections.alt: Adult hands hold a plain peach sunscreen tube beside a notebook on a bright desk.

sections.h2: How Shops Use a First TikTok Ad
paras: A cream shop pastes the product link and gets a tall video of the tube at the seaside. The shoot for that opening stays off the calendar.
A sunscreen shop opens on the tube over a notebook, large enough to see the cap, and posts that file on TikTok.
They write the price and the line in the editor, and pick a song before anyone hears the clip.
They post from the listing photo they already have, after checking the shade against the real tube.

faq.q: What is a practical way to make a TikTok ad?
faq.a: Paste a product link or one photo. You get a tall TikTok ad, with the script and the formatting handled, so you can test an opening without a film crew.

faq.q: Can I make branded TikTok visuals from my own photo?
faq.a: Yes. Start from your photo or your page. The ad can carry your colors, your line, and your product.

faq.q: How quickly can a shop get a first TikTok ad?
faq.a: You can have a TikTok-ready ad in minutes. Paste a product link or a photo. The script, the visuals, a spoken voice, and the tall shape come back together.

faq.q: How does a product page become a TikTok ad?
faq.a: The page supplies the product title, the photos, and the main benefit. You pick a script and an AI actor, or none. You get a tall video with captions and music, ready to post.

faq.q: What do I get from the sunscreen photo in this guide?
faq.a: A tall file built from the product you already sell. Here the tube is on screen, and a voice says what the cream does.

faq.q: Can I test openings before I book a shoot?
faq.a: Yes. Make several versions, see which first line people watch, and book a filmed spot later if you still want one.

faq.q: What do I gain by making the ad this way?
faq.a: You get the video in minutes, you skip the influencer fee, and you can try more than one opening. The clip can sit in the feed like a creator post.

faq.q: Can I aim different versions at different buyers?
faq.a: Yes. Change the script, the AI actor, and the tone. Keep the product the same. Your ad account shows which file people watched.

faq.q: Can the ad match my shop colors and spoken line?
faq.a: Yes. Set your colors, your line, and your captions. Keep the product large enough to see on a phone.
